item.title: One More Week: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open
[-] Close

Here's some crit:

Central Narrative:

My main concern here is the execution of your narrative, you claim this is an SCP article, yet this appears to lean more towards being a tale. How is all this information portrayed in the article? Interviews, journals, casually in the description, where is it? You mention that there will be an interview but nothing about its contents.

clumsiness on the part of the retrieving agents has let the backpack claim them.

Are these not highly trained and briefed MTF Agents? They're not ones to simply inconveniently fuck up.

backpack is frequently found alone

I imagine a lot of these instances happen while the kid is hitchhiking and he suddenly bursts out bleeding in a car, or while working "odd jobs" or while riding the bus.

This:

even just grabbing the backpack is sufficient

Contradicts this:

Once someone finds and opens the backpack

And this:

Once opened the person opening it is transformed

Frankly, it seems like you have a generally good idea of the story but have no idea how you plan on presenting it in a digestible way to the reader. I'd like to see you expand on the execution side of things and fix some of the plot holes I pointed out.

item.title: I want to create an SCP: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Niko Tashira, per the forum guidelines:

Do not use one thread to seek feedback on multiple ideas.

It would be less difficult for you and reviewers to keep track of posted content and to avoid confusion if your one thread was focused on 1 idea. It would be in your benefit of picking one idea you would like to work with in this thread, as there are multiple factors which would guarantee that none of these ideas will succeed if they all were the focus of this thread.

If you have another idea you would like to work with, please make a separate thread for it, but please do be mindful that each author is limited to posting two new concept threads per week (every 7 days).

Once you have reviewed the guidelines, please edit your post rather than creating a new thread, and if you are having trouble editing, click the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your post. Please feel free to then reach out to a reviewer for your concept: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

item.title: Nechronometer: Re: Nechronometer
item.content:encoded: After some critique and conversation over on IRC, I'm giving this a greenlight. This has a lot of potential as both a tale and the start to a tale series. My main advice going forward would be to ensure that your main characters are well-developed, as that seems to be the focus of both this tale and the series at large.

item.title: One More Week: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
Most people aren't used to the whole "edit the original document every time a change is made"; it's normally assumed you would read the entire thread.

The less legwork for reviewers to do, the more likely reviewers will be willing to look at something in the first place. No one's paid for their time helping out authors.

Again, if you're struggling with the forum guidelines, try using the IRC chatrooms or wikidot private messages.

item.title: One More Week: Re: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
As such, since I'm more worried about what the reviewers say than authors, I'm not sure how valuable that advice would be.

Erm… plenty of our reviewers are established authors, and vice-versa.

Do reviewers haunt the chat rooms or just other authors?

The chatroom #thecritters is specifically dedicated to giving/receiving feedback.

As a general note, this line of conversation has diverged quite a bit from the original topic of your concept for critique; if you have further questions about seeking feedback, please use the Questions Desk forum.

item.title: The innate nature of things.: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info

item.title: The Mother of a Hell-Spawn Goat Fetus: Mod Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Hey Savanac -

An author getting the same feedback from two different people is often times a good thing! It means that the issue is deeper than a single reviewer's feedback, and it can be really helpful to hear that something isn't working for many people.

It's ok for two people to say the same thing, and they may even have unique ways of pointing out the same flaw that allow the author to glean more information and ideas!

item.title: A Canary In The Coal Mine: Re: A Canary In The Coal Mine
item.content:encoded: The narrative has a lot of potential. The logic might need some work however. Why would Dr. Gables draw attention to the disasters he was involved in, then go insane and assault the researcher he was trying to get designated as an SCP? If he's trying to eliminate someone who could find out that he was going to do something before he did it, why give credit to the correlation by designating him an SCP? Solid idea, it just seems like it could use some fine tuning.
